_doc: THE one tunable file for JUMP PADS (D-JUMPPAD-1..9; DESIGN.md section 3.4). A jump pad is a separate entity from the generator's LAUNCH pads (voidgen W.pads, the 'X' line, controller _try_launch_pad): a launch pad throws the player onto a target tile and is load-bearing for reachability; a jump pad flings the player STRAIGHT UP, keeps their horizontal momentum, and refills their MOVEMENT resources only (air jumps, dash + twin dash, glider energy, updraft, ability lock) - never void charges, gold or the beacon shield. Placement is game/terrain/jump_pads.gd place_jump_pads(level, cfg): a pure function of the Level dict, so the level hash still determines the pads without touching the frozen generator's canonical text. A pad is a size_tiles x size_tiles BLOCK of tiles (3x3, D-JUMPPAD-6) anchored on its centre tile, and it sits OUTSIDE the paths: every tile of the block is a FLOOR tile of a platform piece, so no tile is a walkway tile (the path) or a walkway's centre lane (the route), and none is the hub/beacon piece, a stair/step/ramp walkway, a ramp tile, a prop, a gift slot, a tripmine slot, a launch pad or its landing tile. Placement prefers the blocks NEAREST the path (D-JUMPPAD-7): candidates are ordered by their XZ gap to the nearest walkway tile within path_step_hu vertically, nearest first, ties broken by the pad RNG stream, then taken greedily with min_spacing_tiles and at most one pad per platform piece. count_by_level: the row with the largest 'from' <= the level number gives the pad count (2 at level 1 up to 6 on big levels; fewer are placed when the level has fewer legal spots, never more). min_spacing_tiles: the XZ distance between any two pad anchors is at least this (a 3x3 pad is 9 tiles, so 8 keeps two pads clearly apart while still fitting 6 on a big level; the old 12 was tuned for 1-tile pads and starved the big levels). path_step_hu: how far above or below a pad's height a walkway tile may sit and still count as the path beside it (the generator steps a walkway 1-2 HU off its parent platform at the junction, and stairs climb 2 HU per row). launch_speed: the upward velocity in u/s set on trigger; under gravity 32 the apex is v^2/64 = 6.25 u at 20.0 (a normal jump is 12.0 -> 2.25 u; a stair walkway climbs at most 3 u, so 6.25 u clears about two stair walkways' worth) and the air time to land back on the pad's height is 2v/32 = 1.25 s. rearm_s: after a pad fires it is inert for this long (rounded to whole 60 Hz ticks), so standing on it cannot chain-fire; landing back on it after a full 1.25 s flight re-fires it, which is the point of a pad.
